>>> help
paper-trails — supported commands

Navigation and inspection
  help                     show this message
  pwd                      print the current directory
  ls [PATH]                list a directory (default: current directory)
  cd [PATH]                change directory (bare `cd` returns to /)
  cat PATH...              print text file contents
  stat PATH                show size, permissions, and modification time

Searching
  grep [-n] PATTERN PATH   search one text file; -n prints line numbers

Forensic tools
  strings [-n LEN] PATH    printable ASCII runs (default minimum length: 4)
  hexdump PATH             hex + ASCII dump, 16 bytes per row
  sha256sum PATH           print the SHA-256 digest of a file
  decode hex|base64 VALUE  decode hex or standard base64 text

Investigation
  evidence                   list recorded evidence and case objectives
  timeline                   show dated evidence in chronological order
  submit who|did|why TEXT    record a line of your final report
  submit                     evaluate the report you have recorded

Notes
  - Every path lives inside the simulated case filesystem. The host
    operating system is never read or executed.
  - Observations are recorded when a command actually surfaces relevant
    case content; run `evidence` to review your journal at any time.
  - grep searches a single file (directories are not searched yet).
  - Paths that climb above / with `..` are rejected as traversal attempts.
  - Quotes group arguments, e.g.: grep -n "failed login" /var/log/auth.log
  - decode prints valid UTF-8 as text; other bytes are shown explicitly,
    e.g.: (bytes) 7f 45
=== end ===

>>> evidence
CASE-001 evidence: 7 of 8

EV-002  Password login for elias from an external address
        sshd accepted a password login for elias from 203.0.113.77 at 23:47:12 — his only password login in the logs. Elias normally authenticates with a public key from 10.0.4.12, and his internal session had closed at 21:31.
        source: /var/log/auth.log
        related: EV-001, EV-003

EV-001  Badge exit after hours
        Badge reader records elias.voss leaving HQ at 21:28:04 on Oct 27 with no later entry — he never badged back in.
        source: /var/log/badge.log
        related: EV-002

EV-004  Host reloaded with export enabled
        syslog records the export pipeline enabled at 23:54:09 with endpoint ingest.pinehill-partners.example under uid=1001 (elias), right after atlas-build installed engine build 0.9.3-export at 23:53:31.
        source: /var/log/syslog
        related: EV-003, EV-005, EV-007

EV-003  Export enabled by commit 7c4e0b9
        The repository reflog shows commit 7c4e0b9 authored as elias@atlas.example at 23:51:40: "config: enable nightly export for pilot partners (OPS-482)" — the same ticket that had declared export disabled on Oct 26.
        source: /home/elias/atlas-repo/.git/logs/HEAD
        related: EV-002, EV-004, EV-006

EV-006  Release documentation declares export disabled
        Release 1.0 candidate notes state the export pipeline is disabled until compliance sign-off (OPS-482); README.txt was last modified 2024-10-26 09:14:02 UTC, matching the Oct 26 docs commit.
        source: /opt/atlas/README.txt
        related: EV-003, EV-005

EV-005  Executable contains enabled-export strings
        Printable strings in engine.bin include export_enabled=1 and endpoint=https://ingest.pinehill-partners.example/v1 — configuration that the release documentation declares disabled.
        source: /opt/atlas/engine.bin
        related: EV-004, EV-006, EV-007

EV-007  Executable modified after the documented release
        stat shows engine.bin modified at 2024-10-27 23:53:31 UTC — after the Oct 26 release notes and seconds before the export pipeline was enabled.
        source: /opt/atlas/engine.bin
        related: EV-004, EV-005

Objectives:

  [x] Identify the configuration change
